need: get an alert from each switch the moment one of its interfaces goes down
clues: the monitoring server should not have to poll every device every minute
the switch itself must send the message when the event happens
the alert must reach the network management system over UDP
appliesWhen: a device must push an event notice to the NMS without being polled
explanation: Traps are messages that an SNMP agent sends on its own when a set event happens, so the NMS learns of the failure at once instead of at its next poll.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: monitor the core routers without sending the management credentials in plain text
clues: the old setup uses plaintext community strings
the auditors require authentication with a username
the polled data must be encrypted on the wire
appliesWhen: the monitoring traffic needs user authentication and encryption
explanation: SNMPv3 adds user-based authentication, message integrity, and encryption, which v2c with its plaintext community strings does not have.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: read the values of a new vendor-specific temperature sensor from the NMS
clues: the NMS already polls the device's standard interface counters
the sensor values appear only as long numeric object IDs
the vendor publishes a file that names each object

answer.item: The vendor's management information base (MIB) loaded into the NMS

appliesWhen: the NMS must learn the names and meaning of a device's managed objects
explanation: The MIB defines the objects a device exposes and maps each OID to a name, so loading the vendor's MIB lets the NMS read and label the new sensor.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: see which hosts and applications use the most bandwidth on the WAN link
clues: storing the full content of every packet is not possible
the router can export a summary record for each conversation
the report must show source, destination, ports, and byte counts

answer.item: Flow data such as NetFlow or IPFIX

appliesWhen: the need is a summary of who talks to whom and how much, not packet contents
explanation: Flow records summarize each conversation by addresses, ports, and volume, which shows the top talkers without capturing full packets.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: examine every field of the frames in a failing application handshake
clues: summary counters show that the traffic reaches the server
the developers need to see the payload and the header flags
the problem happens every time the client connects

answer.item: A packet capture with a protocol analyzer

appliesWhen: the full headers and payload of individual packets must be inspected
explanation: A packet capture records whole frames so a protocol analyzer such as Wireshark can decode every header and the payload of the handshake.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: be notified when traffic on the internet link moves far outside its normal level
clues: usage has been recorded for a month of normal business days
a fixed threshold gives too many false alarms at month end
the team wants a message only for unusual behavior
appliesWhen: alerts must fire when current values differ from what is normal for the network
explanation: A baseline records what normal looks like, and anomaly alerting compares current metrics against it, so only real departures from normal raise a notice.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: keep the log messages from every router and switch in one place
clues: each device keeps only a small log buffer that is lost on reboot
the messages must keep their severity levels
the devices can send their messages over UDP port 514
appliesWhen: device log messages only need to be gathered and stored on one server
explanation: A syslog collector receives and stores log messages from many devices, so the logs survive reboots and can be searched in one place.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: correlate events from the firewalls, servers, and switches to detect attacks in real time
clues: logs from many kinds of systems must be analyzed together
the security team wants a dashboard with drill-down views
a single failed login is normal but a pattern across devices is not

answer.item: A security information and event management (SIEM) system

appliesWhen: security events from many sources must be correlated and analyzed, not only stored
explanation: A SIEM aggregates logs from many sources and correlates them to find threat patterns that no single log shows, with real-time alerts and dashboards.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: open a help desk ticket automatically whenever the monitoring platform raises an alert
clues: the ticketing system accepts requests from other software
staff now copy each alert into a ticket by hand
the ticket must include the device name and the alert text

answer.item: API integration between the monitoring platform and the ticketing system

appliesWhen: the monitoring tool must exchange data with another system or start an automated workflow
explanation: API integration lets the monitoring platform call the ticketing system directly, so each alert creates a ticket with no manual steps.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: send a copy of all traffic on the database server's switch port to an IDS sensor
clues: the sensor must not sit inline with the server's traffic
the switch normally sends frames only to the port of the destination
the sensor is cabled to a spare port on the same switch
appliesWhen: traffic from one switch port must be copied to another port for analysis
explanation: Port mirroring copies the frames of a source port to a monitor port, so a sensor sees the traffic without affecting the server's connection.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: find out right now which devices are on a segment that a contractor just connected
clues: the network inventory has no entries for that segment
the answer is needed today for a troubleshooting call
a ping sweep and port scan of the subnet are allowed

answer.item: An ad hoc network discovery scan

appliesWhen: a one-time discovery is needed for a specific segment or problem
explanation: Ad hoc discovery is a targeted scan run when needed, which finds the devices on that segment at once.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: keep the device inventory and the topology map current without manual work
clues: devices are added and removed every week
the map was last updated by hand six months ago
the scan should repeat automatically at night
appliesWhen: the inventory must be refreshed automatically on a recurring basis
explanation: Scheduled discovery rescans the network at set times, so new and removed devices show up in the inventory without anyone starting a scan.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: find the congestion points and unusual traffic patterns across the network
clues: users report slow transfers only at certain hours
the team needs to see how data moves between sites over time
the cause may be one link or one group of hosts
appliesWhen: the patterns and behavior of the traffic itself must be studied to find bottlenecks
explanation: Traffic analysis examines how traffic moves through the network and when, which shows where congestion and odd patterns occur.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: track latency, jitter, and packet loss on the voice links over time
clues: calls sound choppy on some afternoons
the links never go fully down
the team needs graphs of how well the links carry traffic
appliesWhen: metrics such as latency, jitter, throughput, and loss must be tracked over time
explanation: Performance monitoring tracks quality metrics such as latency, jitter, and loss, which show when a link that is still up is carrying traffic badly.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: know at once when the public web servers stop responding and report their uptime each month
clues: the service level agreement promises 99.9 percent uptime
the managers want a monthly report of any downtime
the check must run every minute from outside the servers
appliesWhen: the main need is to know whether services are up and to report uptime
explanation: Availability monitoring checks that devices and services respond and records uptime, so outages are found quickly and SLA reports can be made.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

need: detect any change to the router and firewall settings that drifts from the approved standard
clues: a golden configuration is stored for each device type
an unapproved change caused an outage last quarter
the auditors want proof that devices match the policy
appliesWhen: device settings must be tracked and compared against a baseline or policy
explanation: Configuration monitoring compares the running settings of devices with the approved baseline and flags drift, which supports change control and audits.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: the new switch answers ping from the monitoring server
the NMS shows the switch as not responding to queries
older switches with the standard setup are polled without problems
the installer typed a custom read-only password on the new switch

answer.cause: a community string on the switch that does not match the one on the NMS
answer.action: Set the same community string on the switch and in the NMS

firstStep: Compare the community string set on the switch with the one in the NMS
appliesWhen: the device and the NMS are set with different SNMP community strings
explanation: In SNMPv2c the community string works like a password, so the agent ignores queries that carry a different one even though the device is reachable.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: polling of the router stopped right after it was hardened
the hardening guide allows only the newest secure protocol version
the router logs show rejected requests that carry no username
the NMS profile for the router has not been changed in years

answer.cause: an NMS that still polls with SNMPv2c while the router accepts only SNMPv3
answer.action: Change the NMS profile for the router to SNMPv3 with the router's user credentials

appliesWhen: the device accepts only SNMPv3 but the NMS still uses v2c
explanation: After hardening, the router drops v2c requests, which carry a community string but no user, so the NMS must use SNMPv3 with a username and keys.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: the NMS shows the new firewall's sensor values as long numeric object IDs
basic interface counters display with normal names
the firewall is from a vendor the NMS has not monitored before

answer.cause: a vendor MIB that is not loaded on the NMS
answer.action: Load the vendor's MIB into the NMS

appliesWhen: the NMS lacks the MIB that names a device's vendor-specific objects
explanation: Standard MIBs cover the interface counters, but vendor objects need the vendor's MIB so the NMS can translate the OIDs into names.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: every device at the branch stopped reporting to the NMS at the same time
a new rule set was applied to the branch firewall yesterday
the NMS can still reach the branch devices by SSH

answer.cause: a firewall rule that blocks UDP ports 161 and 162 between the NMS and the branch
answer.action: Allow UDP 161 and 162 between the NMS and the branch devices on the firewall

firstStep: Review the firewall rules that were changed yesterday
appliesWhen: a firewall between the NMS and the devices blocks the SNMP ports
explanation: All devices failed together right after a firewall change while SSH still works, which points to the SNMP ports being blocked, not to the devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: the collector receives emergency and alert messages from the switch
interface flap warnings show on the switch console but never on the collector
other switches send their warnings to the collector

answer.cause: a logging level on the switch that sends only critical and more severe messages
answer.action: Lower the switch's logging threshold so that warning-level messages are sent

firstStep: Check the logging level set for the remote log host on the switch
appliesWhen: the device's logging threshold is set above the level of the missing messages
explanation: Syslog sends only messages at or above the set severity, so warnings (level 4) are dropped when the threshold is critical (level 2).
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: no messages from the router have reached the collector since the logging server moved
other devices that were updated last week still log normally
the router's local buffer shows many recent events

answer.cause: a router configuration that still names the old log server address
answer.action: Update the logging host address on the router to the new collector

appliesWhen: the device still sends its log messages to an old or wrong server address
explanation: The router creates events but sends them nowhere useful, because its logging host still points to the address the collector used before the move.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: the analyzer is cabled to the switch's monitor port and shows traffic
none of the captured frames come from or go to the file server
the session was copied from a template for another rack

answer.cause: a SPAN session that copies the wrong source port
answer.action: Set the session's source to the file server's switch port

firstStep: Check which source port the mirror session copies
appliesWhen: the mirror session copies traffic from a port other than the one under study
explanation: The analyzer gets mirrored frames, so the session works, but it copies another port's traffic, which means the source is set wrong.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: anomaly alerts fire every morning since 200 new staff joined
the alerting system has not been retuned in two years
the traffic peaks match the new normal start of the work day

answer.cause: an outdated baseline that no longer matches normal network traffic
answer.action: Record a new baseline of normal traffic and retune the alert thresholds

appliesWhen: normal traffic has grown and the reference data that alerts use is old
explanation: Anomaly alerts compare traffic with a baseline, so after normal usage grows, an old baseline flags normal traffic as unusual.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations

clues: new laptops get 169.254.x.x addresses
devices that were already on the network keep working
the office grew from 120 to 260 staff this month
the address range was sized for a /25 years ago

answer.cause: an exhausted DHCP scope with no free addresses
answer.action: Enlarge the scope or add an address range for the subnet

firstStep: Check how many free addresses are left in the scope
appliesWhen: every address in the pool is already leased to a client
explanation: Only new clients fail and fall back to APIPA after the staff count doubled, which shows the pool has no addresses left to lease.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: clients on the new VLAN get 169.254.x.x addresses
the address server sits on a different subnet in the data center
clients on the server's own subnet get leases normally
the scope for the new VLAN exists and has free addresses

answer.cause: a router interface for the new VLAN with no IP helper address
answer.action: Configure an IP helper (DHCP relay) on the new VLAN's router interface that points to the DHCP server

firstStep: Check the router interface of the new VLAN for an IP helper address
appliesWhen: clients are on a subnet without a relay to the remote DHCP server
explanation: DHCP discovery is a broadcast that routers do not forward, so clients on a remote subnet need a relay agent to reach the server.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: some clients get 192.168.0.x addresses instead of the company 10.10.x.x range
those clients have a gateway the company does not use and cannot reach servers
a user plugged a home wireless router into a wall jack this morning

answer.cause: an unauthorized DHCP server on the network
answer.action: Find and disconnect the unauthorized server and enable DHCP snooping on the switches

appliesWhen: a second, unauthorized server is handing out leases with the wrong settings
explanation: Clients that get a foreign address range and gateway took a lease from another server, here the home router that a user connected.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: a duplicate address warning appears on a PC
the same address is set by hand on a network printer
the printer's address is inside the range the server hands out

answer.cause: a static printer address that is not excluded from the DHCP scope
answer.action: Add an exclusion to the scope for the addresses that are set by hand

firstStep: Check whether the conflicting address is in the scope's pool
appliesWhen: a statically set address is still inside the pool that the server leases
explanation: The server leased an address that a printer already uses because nothing told it to skip that address; an exclusion removes it from the pool.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: clients get addresses in the right subnet
clients can reach local servers but not the internet
a PC with a manually set address in the same subnet works
an administrator edited the scope settings yesterday

answer.cause: a wrong router (default gateway) option in the DHCP scope
answer.action: Correct the router option in the scope and have clients renew their leases

firstStep: Compare the gateway that a client received with the router's real address
appliesWhen: the scope hands out a wrong default gateway address
explanation: Local traffic works and only off-subnet traffic fails for DHCP clients, which points to the gateway the scope gives out.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: clients can ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot open websites by name
setting a name server by hand on one PC fixes that PC
every client that gets its settings automatically has the problem

answer.cause: a wrong DNS server option in the DHCP scope
answer.action: Correct the DNS server option in the scope and renew the clients' leases

appliesWhen: the scope gives clients a wrong name server address
explanation: Clients reach the internet by IP address but not by name, and a manual name server fixes it, so the server address from DHCP is wrong.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: hosts have only fe80:: addresses on the new IPv6 segment
the design uses stateless autoconfiguration with no DHCPv6 server
the router interface has the global prefix configured

answer.cause: router advertisements that are suppressed on the router interface
answer.action: Enable router advertisements for the prefix on the router interface

firstStep: Check whether the router interface sends router advertisements
appliesWhen: hosts never receive the router advertisements that carry the prefix
explanation: SLAAC hosts build global addresses from the prefix in router advertisements, so with advertisements suppressed they keep only link-local addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: the guest address pool runs out by midday
most guests stay less than an hour
addresses stay assigned for eight days after a visitor leaves

answer.cause: a lease time that is much too long for short guest visits
answer.action: Shorten the lease time on the guest scope to a few hours

appliesWhen: addresses stay tied to clients that left long ago
explanation: A client keeps its address until the lease ends, so with eight-day leases and short visits the pool fills with addresses no one uses.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: users suddenly cannot print to the printer by its IP address
the printer's panel shows a different address than last week
the printer gets its settings automatically

answer.cause: a printer with no DHCP reservation that received a new address
answer.action: Create a DHCP reservation for the printer's MAC address and update the print queues

firstStep: Compare the address on the printer's panel with the address in the print queue
appliesWhen: a device that needs a fixed address gets whatever address is free
explanation: Without a reservation the printer can get a different address when it renews, which breaks queues that point to its old address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: make sure the new network printer always gets the same address
clues: the printer must stay a DHCP client
the address must be tied to the printer's MAC address
the print queues on every PC use the printer's IP address
appliesWhen: one device must always get the same address from the server
explanation: A reservation ties an address to a client's MAC address, so the printer still uses DHCP but always gets the same address.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: stop the server from leasing the addresses that the servers and switches use
clues: those devices have addresses set by hand
the addresses sit inside the range of the subnet's pool
the devices must not depend on the DHCP server
appliesWhen: some addresses inside the pool must never be handed out
explanation: An exclusion removes addresses from the pool, so the server never leases the addresses already set by hand.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: serve addresses to five VLANs from one central DHCP server
clues: the server sits in the data center subnet
routers do not forward broadcasts between the VLANs
the company does not want a DHCP server in each VLAN

answer.item: A DHCP relay agent (IP helper) on each VLAN's router interface

appliesWhen: clients on other subnets must reach a central DHCP server
explanation: A relay agent forwards the clients' broadcast requests to the central server as unicast, so one server can serve every VLAN.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: let IPv6 hosts build their own global addresses with no server that tracks them
clues: the router advertises the /64 prefix on the segment
no one wants to keep a lease database for the segment
the hosts can form an interface ID on their own
appliesWhen: IPv6 hosts must configure addresses from the router's prefix without a stateful server
explanation: With SLAAC a host takes the prefix from router advertisements and adds its own interface ID, so no server has to track the addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: give every client its gateway, name servers, and domain suffix automatically
clues: the clients already get their addresses from the server
technicians set the gateway and name servers by hand today
the values are the same for every client in the subnet
appliesWhen: extra settings such as gateway, DNS servers, or suffix must be handed out with the address
explanation: Scope options send settings such as the default gateway, DNS servers, and DNS suffix along with each lease.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: reuse addresses quickly on the guest wireless network
clues: hundreds of visitors connect each day for less than an hour
the pool is a single /24
addresses now stay assigned for days after a visitor leaves

answer.item: A short lease time on the guest scope

appliesWhen: addresses must return to the pool soon after clients leave
explanation: A short lease returns unused addresses to the pool quickly, which suits many brief visitors on a small pool.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: hand out addresses in the new 10.20.30.0/24 subnet from the existing server
clues: the server already serves two other subnets
requests from the new subnet already reach the server
the server has no address range for that subnet yet

answer.item: A new DHCP scope for the 10.20.30.0/24 subnet

appliesWhen: the server needs an address range defined for a subnet it does not serve yet
explanation: A scope defines the range of addresses the server leases for one subnet, so the new subnet needs its own scope.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: let clients find the intranet server's IPv4 address by its host name
clues: the server has the address 10.1.5.20
users type intranet.example.com
the network uses only IPv4 for this server
appliesWhen: a host name must map to an IPv4 address
explanation: An A record maps a host name to an IPv4 address, which is the forward lookup the clients need.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: let clients reach the web server by name over IPv6
clues: the server has the address 2001:db8:10::25
clients that have only IPv6 addresses must reach it by name
the IPv4 name mapping already exists
appliesWhen: a host name must map to an IPv6 address
explanation: An AAAA (quad-A) record maps a host name to a 128-bit IPv6 address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: make shop.example.com another name for the server www.example.com
clues: the server already has its own name mapping
the alias must follow the server if its address changes
no second address is needed
appliesWhen: one name must be an alias of another host name
explanation: A CNAME record points an alias to the canonical name, so the alias always follows the real host's address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: tell other companies' mail servers which host accepts email for the domain
clues: the new mail gateway is mail2.example.com
outside senders look up the domain, not a host name
a backup gateway should get a lower priority
appliesWhen: a domain must name the servers that receive its email
explanation: An MX record lists the mail servers for a domain, with a preference value that sets their order.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: publish the list of servers allowed to send email for the domain
clues: the entry is free-form text that starts with v=spf1
a cloud service also asks for a verification token
the entry does not map a name to an address
appliesWhen: free-form text such as SPF, DKIM, DMARC, or a verification token must be published
explanation: A TXT record holds free-form text; SPF policies and domain verification tokens are published this way.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: delegate the branch.example.com subdomain to the branch's own name servers
clues: the branch servers will be authoritative for the subdomain
the parent zone must point queries to them
the branch servers already host the subdomain's zone
appliesWhen: a zone must name the authoritative servers for itself or a subdomain
explanation: An NS record names the authoritative name servers, and NS records in the parent zone delegate a subdomain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: let the mail gateway find a host name from the sending server's IP address
clues: the lookup starts from an address, not a name
the entry goes in the in-addr.arpa zone
receiving servers check that the address maps back to a name
appliesWhen: an IP address must map back to a host name
explanation: A PTR record holds the address-to-name mapping used by reverse lookups.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: keep a read-only copy of the company zone on a second server for redundancy
clues: the master copy stays on the first server
the copy must update through zone transfers
users must resolve names if the first server fails
appliesWhen: a read-only copy of a zone must be kept by zone transfer
explanation: A secondary zone holds a read-only copy that it receives from the primary by zone transfer, so a second server can answer if the first fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: create the zone that will hold the address-to-name entries for the 10.1.0.0/16 network
clues: the zone name ends in in-addr.arpa
lookups start from an IP address
the existing zone holds only name-to-address entries
appliesWhen: a zone must hold address-to-name mappings
explanation: A reverse zone, named under in-addr.arpa, holds the PTR records that map addresses back to names.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: hold the one writable master copy of the company's zone
clues: all record changes must be made on one server
other servers will copy from it
its serial number goes up with each change
appliesWhen: the writable master copy of a zone is needed
explanation: The primary zone is the writable master copy; secondary servers copy it from there.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: let internal clients look up any internet name through one company server
clues: the clients must not query internet name servers themselves
the server must follow referrals from the root down
answers should be cached for other clients
appliesWhen: a server must do the full lookup for clients and cache the answers
explanation: A recursive resolver queries the root, TLD, and authoritative servers on the client's behalf and caches the results.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: store the records that map the company's host names to IP addresses
clues: clients search by name and need an address back
the domain is example.com
the records will be mostly A and AAAA entries
appliesWhen: a zone must hold name-to-address mappings
explanation: A forward lookup zone holds the records that map names to addresses, such as A and AAAA records.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: let resolvers verify that the answers from the company's zone are authentic and unchanged
clues: attackers have tried to poison caches with false answers
the records must carry digital signatures
the queries themselves do not need to be private
appliesWhen: DNS answers must be signed so resolvers can check their origin and integrity
explanation: DNSSEC signs the zone's records, so a validating resolver can prove an answer came from the zone and was not changed; it does not encrypt the queries.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: keep the laptops' name lookups private from anyone on hotel and airport networks
clues: the lookups now cross the network in plain text
the queries must be encrypted between the laptop and the resolver
the traffic may travel over port 443 or port 853

answer.item: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) or DNS over TLS (DoT)

appliesWhen: the DNS queries themselves must be encrypted in transit
explanation: DoH and DoT wrap DNS queries in HTTPS or TLS, which hides them from others on the local network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: point one test PC to the staging web server by its normal name without changing any name server
clues: only this one PC must use the staging address
other users must still reach the live site
the developer has local administrator rights

answer.item: An entry in the PC's hosts file

appliesWhen: a single computer must resolve a name locally without DNS
explanation: The hosts file is checked before DNS, so an entry there changes the name's address on that PC only.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

clues: the intranet server moved to a new IP address an hour ago
most users reach the site
one PC still tries to connect to the old address
nslookup on that PC returns the new address from the server

answer.cause: a stale cached entry in the client's DNS resolver cache
answer.action: Flush the client's DNS cache with ipconfig /flushdns

appliesWhen: the client still holds an old lookup result in its local cache
explanation: The server already returns the new address, so the PC is using an old answer it cached before the move; flushing the cache clears it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

clues: other companies' servers reject the outgoing email
the bounce message says the sender's address has no matching host name
lookups of the server's name return the right address

answer.cause: a missing PTR record for the mail server's public IP address
answer.action: Add a PTR record for the mail server's address in the reverse zone

firstStep: Run a reverse lookup on the mail server's public IP address
appliesWhen: the server's IP address does not map back to a host name
explanation: Many mail servers check that the sender's address maps back to a name; forward lookups work, so the reverse entry is the part missing.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

clues: only one PC still reaches the old intranet server
flushing the resolver cache does not help
nslookup on that PC shows the correct new address
a contractor tested the site on that PC months ago

answer.cause: an old static entry in the PC's hosts file
answer.action: Remove the outdated entry from the hosts file

firstStep: Open the PC's hosts file and look for an entry for the server
appliesWhen: a local static entry overrides the DNS answer on that computer
explanation: nslookup asks the name server directly, but applications check the hosts file first, so a leftover entry wins on that PC even after a cache flush.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

clues: internal email between staff works
messages from outside senders stopped arriving after the migration
the old gateway was shut down last week
outside senders get a delivery delay notice

answer.cause: an MX record that still points to the old mail gateway
answer.action: Update the MX record to the new mail gateway's host name

firstStep: Look up the domain's MX record from an outside resolver
appliesWhen: the domain's mail exchanger entry names a server that no longer accepts mail
explanation: Outside servers find where to deliver mail from the domain's MX record, so after the migration they still try the old, shut-down gateway.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

clues: new host names resolve on one name server but not on the other
the serial number on the second server has not changed in days
the first server's settings were hardened last week

answer.cause: zone transfers from the primary to the secondary server that are now refused
answer.action: Allow zone transfers to the secondary server's address on the primary

firstStep: Compare the zone serial numbers on the two servers
appliesWhen: the secondary can no longer copy the zone from the primary
explanation: The secondary still serves an old copy because its serial number does not change, which shows it is no longer getting zone transfers from the primary.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

clues: validating resolvers return SERVFAIL for the company domain
resolvers that do not validate still get answers
the scheduled key rollover and re-signing job failed last month

answer.cause: expired DNSSEC signatures on the zone
answer.action: Re-sign the zone and publish fresh signatures and keys

appliesWhen: the zone's signatures have expired so validating resolvers reject its answers
explanation: Only validating resolvers fail, which means the answers exist but their signatures cannot be trusted, here because the re-signing job failed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing

need: keep the clocks of all servers, switches, and firewalls within a few milliseconds of one reference
clues: log entries from many devices must line up
millisecond accuracy is enough
the devices can reach the company's time servers over UDP 123
appliesWhen: ordinary devices need millisecond-level clock sync
explanation: NTP syncs clocks over UDP port 123 through a hierarchy of strata, which gives millisecond accuracy for logs and authentication.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: sync the trading servers' clocks to within a microsecond
clues: each trade must carry a timestamp more precise than a millisecond
the switches support hardware timestamping
one grandmaster clock will lead the others
appliesWhen: clocks need sub-microsecond accuracy
explanation: PTP (IEEE 1588) syncs clocks to a grandmaster with hardware timestamps and reaches sub-microsecond accuracy.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: stop attackers from spoofing or changing the time updates the servers receive
clues: a test showed that forged time packets were accepted
the clients must verify that each time update is genuine
the existing time protocol should stay in use
appliesWhen: time sync traffic must be authenticated against spoofing and tampering
explanation: NTS (RFC 8915) adds cryptographic protection to NTP so clients can trust that time updates are genuine and unchanged.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

need: provide accurate time to an isolated network with no internet access
clues: outside time servers cannot be reached
the building has a roof antenna with a clear view of the sky
all devices must still agree on the correct time of day

answer.item: A local time server with a GPS reference clock

appliesWhen: the network needs its own accurate time source without reaching outside servers
explanation: A GPS receiver serves as a stratum 0 reference, so a local server attached to it can act as stratum 1 for the isolated network.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: the user cannot sign in to the domain from one PC
other users sign in without problems
the PC's taskbar shows a time 20 minutes behind the wall clock
the sign-in error mentions a ticket that is not yet valid

answer.cause: a PC clock that is too far off the domain controller's time
answer.action: Set the PC to sync with the domain's time source and resync it

firstStep: Compare the PC's time with the domain controller's time
appliesWhen: the computer's clock differs from the authentication server by more than the allowed skew
explanation: Kerberos tickets carry timestamps and are rejected when clocks differ by more than about five minutes, so a PC that is 20 minutes off cannot sign in.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: the internal time server's offset grows a little each day
the server reports that none of its upstream sources are reachable
a new perimeter firewall was installed last week

answer.cause: a firewall that blocks UDP port 123 to the upstream time sources
answer.action: Allow UDP 123 from the internal time server to its upstream sources

firstStep: Check the firewall rules for UDP 123 from the time server
appliesWhen: the time server cannot reach its upstream sources through the firewall
explanation: The internal server drifts because it can no longer reach its sources, and the change came with a new firewall, which points to NTP's port being blocked.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: events in the SIEM appear in the wrong order
one switch's entries are seven minutes ahead of the firewall's
each device's clock was set by hand when it was installed

answer.cause: devices that do not sync to a common time source
answer.action: Configure every device to use the same NTP servers

appliesWhen: devices keep their own clocks instead of syncing to one source
explanation: Clocks set by hand drift apart, so log times from different devices do not line up; a common NTP source fixes the order.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching

clues: the servers' clocks jump by hours at random
each jump follows packets from an unknown host that claims to be a time source
the time clients accept any update without checking it

answer.cause: forged time updates from a rogue host that the clients trust
answer.action: Enable Network Time Security so clients accept only authenticated time updates

appliesWhen: an attacker sends false time updates that the clients cannot verify
explanation: The clocks jump only when packets arrive from an unknown host, and nothing checks the updates, so forged time is the cause; NTS authenticates them.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
